As a consequence, I probably have a lot of incorrect and ignorant ideas floating around in my head (it is far easier to simplify things than to get to the truth). The difference between me (I hope I am wrong, but I know this to be true) and the average Redditor is that I am constantly looking to better my knowledge and to truly test these ideas.

I will not really settle down on an opinion/view until I have researched the hell out of it. Then I will, as a man should, hold this view strongly and spread it. For example, I had always known that science and religion did not go together. Reddit, normal media, teachers and friends have made this an apparent fact. Little side comments and anecdotes, historical fables and interesting "facts" are trotted out throughout the course of decades.

It seems to make sense.

So chance has it that you meet a stranger. After a small conversation he asserts that one such anecdote is false! Preposterous. You laugh at him and say it is common knowledge, and so you do a quick Google search. Which turns into a long research session, which turns into an obsession. The stranger was right. The anecdote never happened; the fact was a fable. Everyone had been regurgitating unbased nonsense. Not only that, there are many such falsehoods, and sometimes the falsehoods are even presented falsely themselves!

The church had not banned zero. Zero people burned at the stake for their scientific views. Galileo was not tortured.

So you dig a little deeper. And deeper. You start to find yourself wander in the complete opposite direction -the church was right and more scientific and rational than Galileo! So you must drag yourself to only the facts and no speculation; as all else have done. (Sidenote: that is again, another simplification, but the church appears to have been more scientifically proper than Galileo, according to modern scholarship).

After some searching you will find the truth is never simple. It is always much more complex than that. Simplifications are very easy to fall into; they appeal to the lazy and the uncaring. The best way to combat this is to never get "comfy" with a view. Always poke holes. Prove to yourself that what you believe is true is not regurgitated nonsense.

Again, I have gone on about a single case study of science and religion (search Wikipedia for "conflict thesis" to see what I am on about, if you are interested). These knots took me months to fully knead out. I cannot even imagine how many falsehoods I hold true. Hopefully they will be caught out soon and fixed. I'd like to think that I am slightly immune to the herd mentality as I diversify my news/entertainment/tech/etc sources. This makes it harder to get "comfy".

If you wish to get a nibblet of what I am talking about, read this piece about Galileo, the Church, Heliocentrism and Geocentrism (again, yet another simplification!). This is an excellent piece of writing: http://tofspot.blogspot.com.au/2013/08/the-great-ptolemaic-smackdown.html.
